Thank you all for your reports. Let me summarize what I'm hearing and identify the key issues we need to resolve before I can make a decision.

First, Thomas, you mentioned a critical timing issue — please go ahead and share that with the group now, as it may affect everything else.

Second, Nadia, your forensic findings of 23 copied files in the Alpha repository are clearly central to this application. However, Sofia has raised an important insurance requirement: the insurer must consent in writing before we engage an outside forensic expert whose fees will be claimed as covered defense costs. I need to understand — Nadia, was your forensic work done in-house, or did we engage any outside expert? And Sofia, does this consent requirement apply to work already completed, or only to future engagements?

Third, Marcus, the client's position is clear — we seek return and deletion of the 23 copied files and a prohibition on the engineer using those files, but we do NOT seek to bar the engineer from working for the competitor. That sets the scope of our requested relief.

Finally, Sofia, the insurer notice requirement means we cannot file the emergency application until the insurer has been notified. I need to know how quickly that notice can be given and whether we can satisfy it today.

Thomas, please share your timing issue so we can put all of this together.

Thank you, Nadia and Marcus. Let me address the questions directed to me.

First, on the insurer notice: Yes, I can provide notice to the insurer today. The policy endorsement I received yesterday specifies that notice must be given before any court filing, but it does not impose a waiting period after notice. So as long as we send notice and can confirm receipt before the October 9th 5:00 p.m. filing deadline, that requirement can be satisfied within our window.

Second, on the outside expert consent requirement: Since Nadia's forensic work was done entirely in-house, the consent requirement does not apply to her completed work. However, as Nadia correctly flagged, if any independent verification by an outside expert becomes necessary — whether at the court's direction or the insurer's request — we would need to obtain the insurer's written consent before engaging that expert and before claiming those fees as covered defense costs. I cannot confirm at this moment how quickly the insurer would respond to a consent request, as I have not yet contacted them. I recommend we determine whether outside expert verification is likely to be needed as early as possible so I can initiate the consent process immediately if it is.

Elena, from an insurance coverage standpoint, the critical path items are: (1) insurer notice before filing — achievable today; and (2) no outside expert engagement without prior written insurer consent if fees are to be claimed as covered costs. I will prepare and send the coverage note to the group today so everyone has the policy requirements documented.
